newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. approves food entry point on Iraq-Syria border.
newsitem.headline: U.N. approves food entry point on Iraq-Syria border.

text.p: The United Nations has approved a location on the Iraqi-Syrian border as a new entry point for humanitarian goods to Iraq under the "oil-for-food" plan, the Security Council's sanctions committee said on Friday.
The location is at Al-Walid, opposite Al-Tenf in Syria.
Other entry points already in use are the Iraqi port of Umm Qasr, Trebil on the Iraqi-Jordanian border and Zakho on the Iraqi-Turkish border.

A team of U.N. inspection agents will be stationed at the newly-designated site to authenticate the arrival of humanitarian supplies under the "oil-for-food" plan that allows Iraq to export $2 billion worth of oil every six months to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed shortly after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
